name: Peire Vidal
bio: Peire Vidal was a troubadour of Toulouse whom Farnell treats as one of the most colourful figures of the age. The first poem given here is a boastful self-portrait, the second a canzone in praise of love.

The verse in this selection is Ida Farnell's English version in The Lives of the Troubadours (London: David Nutt, 1896), where it stands beside a prose Life of the poet; the prose Life is not reproduced here. The dates are those Farnell prints for the period in which the poet was active, and the Old Occitan original is not included.

poems.title: Poem by Vidal on Himself
poems.author: Peire Vidal
poems.text:
Sir Dragoman, had I a goodly steed,
Soon would my enemies for mercy plead;
For even when they hear of men my name,
They fear me more than quail doth fear hawk's greed;
Nor prize their life a doit, so fierce of deed,
So stern they know me, and so great my fame.

When donned my glitt'ring, steel-lined coat of mail,
And girt my sword, Hugh's gift that cannot fail,
Whither I go, the earth doth shake with fear;
No foes I meet that do not 'fore me pale,
And yield me place; nought doth their pride avail,
So great their terror when my step they hear.

Roland and Oliver in one am I,
With Montdidier in courtesy I vie;
Full often messengers do bear to me
For my great worth and for my valour high,
Gold rings and bands of white and sable dye,
And greetings that fill all my heart with glee.

When vanquished 'fore me jealous mockers kneel,
Who by false semblance would their craft conceal,
And by fair means or foul would joy condemn —
These verily shall learn what blows I deal,
For, be their bodies made of iron or steel,
No peacock's feather shall it profit them.

Of chivalry and love I am the flower,
Bravest among the brave — in lady's bower
Is none more courteous and more debonair,
Nor in the battle-field of greater power,
So that my enemies in terror cower
At thought of me, nor to confront me dare.

poems.title: Canzone
poems.author: Peire Vidal
poems.text:
Great joy have I to greet the season bright,
And joy to greet the blessed summer days,
And joy when birds do carol songs of praise,
And joy to mark the woods with flowerets dight,
And joy at all whereat to joy were meet,
And joy unending at the pleasaunce sweet
That yonder in my joy I think to gain,
There where in joy my soul and sense remain.

'Tis Love that keeps me in such dear delight,
'Tis Love's clear fire that keeps my breast ablaze,
'Tis Love that can my sinking courage raise,
Even for Love am I in grievous plight;
With tender thoughts Love makes my heart to beat,
And o'er my every wish has rule complete —
Virtue I cherish since began his reign,
And to do deeds of Love am ever fain.
